answer_1.quote: We propose ValCAT, which generates high-quality adversarial examples by applying variable-length contextualized transformations to the original text.

answer_2.quote: Metrics We evaluate the effectiveness of ValCAT based on the following metrics: • Attack success rate (Suc): ... • Perplexity (PPL): ... • Semantic similarity (Sim): ... • Word perturbation rate (Pert): ... • Grammar error (GErr): ...

answer_4.quote: Design We evaluate the quality of the adversarial examples from three perspectives: readability (fluency and grammaticality), semantic similarity, and label consistency. ... Five annotators with CET-4 certification performed the evaluation ...
answer_4.guideline: For the evaluation of fluency and grammaticality, each original text and its two adversarial examples are presented in one group in a shuffled order and the annotators are asked to rate them. For the evaluation of semantic similarity, given the original text, the judges need to separately evaluate its semantic similarity with the two adversarial examples presented in random order. ... For the evaluation of label consistency, we mix all the original texts with the adversarial examples and let the annotators label the category of them.
